turn2.differences: The author's three conditions (c1 exact title, c2 description covering a procurement checklist, c3 created in January) match my step 1 reading closely. No condition is missing or added; 'originally created' in c3 correctly targets created_at rather than updated_at, which the record set (hub 9206) specifically tests.

ambiguity_effects.explain: A loose reading (title merely contains the phrase 'Vendor Onboarding') would let 9201 ('Vendor Onboarding EMEA') pass c1 and, combined with its January creation and procurement-checklist description, become a second full match. But the word 'simply' strongly signals an exact-title reading, so under the natural reading only 9200 (and the other exact-title hubs) qualify on c1, and no extra candidate is added.

A very broad reading ('about vendor/procurement matters generally') could arguably let 9203's 'general resources...for new vendor setup' pass, creating a second full match alongside 9200. The natural reading, though, requires the description to actually reference a procurement checklist, which 9203 does not, so this stays a single match.

If read as 'the hub's record was last touched/updated in January' rather than 'created in January', hub 9206 (created October, updated January) would pass c3 and become a second full match. The phrase 'originally created' clearly points to the creation date, so under the natural reading 9206 is excluded and the match set stays unique.

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing is a bit more explicit/verbose than typical casual speech (stacking three qualifiers), but it reads like a real request from someone disambiguating among several similarly-titled hubs they know exist, which matches the data (five hubs titled exactly 'Vendor Onboarding').
